aggregation_weighting.definition: original: per (order, seed, task) normalized_delta = (post_train - independent)/normalizer; family slot = mean over the family's two tasks; per-seed = mean over the four orders; reported mean = mean over the 8 confirmation seeds (scripts/evaluate_multimodal_confirmation.py, transfer_records/transfer_statistics)

decomposition_definition.T: native_diag_normalized - independent_normalized (the reported normalized transfer endpoint)
decomposition_definition.R: native_diag_normalized - oracle_diag_normalized (routing counterfactual: cost of native routing vs own task_id_oracle routing at the diagonal stage, same trained bank)
decomposition_definition.K: oracle_diag_normalized - independent_normalized (training-path difference when routing is held at the own expert)
decomposition_definition.identity: T == R + K holds per bank/task (all three scores from the same eval corpus; verified numerically)
decomposition_definition.score_sources: native/oracle: artifacts/multimodal-g5-report/routing_audit.json variant matrices (previously rescored); independent: artifacts/multimodal-g4-report/audit.json (independent trials; post_train/normalizer); NO scorer executed here

R_own_route_worstcase_bound.what: worst-case max |own-route contribution to R| over all 32 diagonal cells (no scorer execution)
caveats: not a confidence interval and carries no causal claim; per-row error signs and magnitudes stay unknown
applies only to R (native minus oracle on the trained bank); the native-vs-independent subgroup contribution of the own group is not recoverable because the K side is a different comparison
per-group absolute scores remain unavailable without per-example accuracy (never persisted)
text-identical own rows contribute exactly 0 (deterministic scorer), so the bound uses only actually mismatching rows from the files, not a hardcoded count

routing_counterfactual_extent.definition: share of misrouted rows whose own-expert (task_id_oracle) prediction text is byte-equal to the native prediction text; those rows' routing choice is inconsequential for the answer

interpretation.vqa_transfer: T = -0.04324 splits exactly into R = -0.02087 (native routing vs own-expert routing at the diagonal stage, the routing counterfactual) and K = -0.02237 (the stream-trained expert, perfectly routed, still below the same-seed independent run). Code review rules out any parameter-level cross-task source for K (frozen siblings and router are inert during the phase; position-0 tasks have T == R == K == 0 exactly because the first-task stream is byte-identical to the independent run). The remaining cause(s) of nonzero K at positions > 0 are unverified; the seeded protocol difference (different A-init draw streams and batch-shuffle seeds) is one unproven hypothesis, and no causal RNG attribution or 'learned cross-task knowledge' reading is established.
interpretation.caption_transfer: T = +0.02015 = R +0.01586 + K +0.00429. Per task the decomposition is strongly heterogeneous: C is T=-0.0521 (routing deficit R=-0.0511 dominates) while F is T=+0.0924 (R=+0.0828: the oracle-forced F expert differs from native routing and the corpus favors native). The caption aggregate hides this sign structure. [INFERENCE, unverified] the F component is measured against an independent F reference that scores close to its fixed normalizer (0.0999 vs 0.1526 mean CIDEr over seeds), so the positive F transfer may partly reflect a weak independent reference rather than new-task learning.
interpretation.caption_final_stage: Whole-corpus: task_id_oracle caption family final (0.7114) is below native joint (0.7434), and per task oracle beats native for C while losing for F. Per-cell subgroup paired deltas are identified only for eligible cells (0 same-expert text mismatches): per-order eligible seed counts, corpus deltas and counts are in per_task/per_order; pool-level subgroup statistics are unidentifiable whenever any own-route row differs. No cross-family caption routes exist (0 rows across all 32 banks), so the route-differ set equals the same-family-other-expert partition exactly.

vqa_diagonal_partition.definition: all rows of the diagonal-stage VQA prediction files; 'own' = row routed to the task's own expert (assignment index == position in stream); 'mis' = any other expert; text identity against the same-seed independent run and the G5 own-expert counterfactual
vqa_diagonal_partition.identification_note: rows whose native prediction text equals the independent prediction contribute exactly 0 to the transfer delta (deterministic scorer on identical text). Cautions: (a) rows routed to their own expert are not guaranteed to produce identical text in the native and oracle variant files - same-expert text mismatches are counted per task x order below and their source is unknown (one unverified hypothesis is micro-batch composition effects on bf16 greedy near-ties); (b) per-example accuracy is not persisted anywhere, so the magnitude split inside each group is not identifiable without re-running the scorer - only the max-magnitude bounds below and the exact corpus-level R/K split above are available

caption_final_stage.definition: final stream stage; per C/F row the native expert is own-task expert, same-family other caption expert, or cross-family (validated); native/oracle corpus CIDEr-D come from the G5 audit; whole-corpus native-minus-oracle deltas and counts are reported for every C/F x order x seed. The selected-group mean paired delta is IDENTIFIED ONLY for bank/task cells with zero own-route text mismatches (reported 'group_paired_delta_identified'); for any cell with a same-expert text difference the whole-cohort subgroup absolute scores and paired differences stay unidentifiable. Own-route rows are predictions of the same expert weights in both variants, but equal outputs are an observation made per bank, not a guaranteed identity (source of observed mismatches unknown).

all_orders.ownership_note: see per-order eligible coverage; pool-level subgroup stats are unidentifiable
see per-order eligible coverage; pool-level subgroup stats are unidentifiable

own_route_generation_numerics.explanation: two generation runs of the same trained bank on the same expert and the same rows are not bitwise-guaranteed; the source of the observed same-expert text differences is unknown. One unverified hypothesis is micro-batch-composition-dependent bf16 rounding of near-tied greedy tokens (readout_model.py generate(), run.py routed_predictions grouping); counts are exact, causal attribution is not established.
own_route_generation_numerics.consequence: same-expert rows may contribute nonzero (c_native - c_oracle) even when they are routed to their own expert in both variants; pool-level subgroup statistics are therefore unidentifiable whenever any same-expert row differs, and the exact selected-group mean is retained only for eligible cells (0 own-route text mismatches).

family_normalized_final.not_equal_to_g4_final_stage: final-stage values are diagonal-free summaries of the shipped G5 audit

unidentifiable_without_new_scoring: per-group absolute native CIDEr-D mean (mean of per-image native contributions over the group)
paired-difference distributions within the route-differ group
pool-level (whole-task) subgroup means and paired differences whenever any own-route row of the pool differs textually between the variants
decomposition of a same-expert text mismatch into native-vs-oracle score gaps on that row
caption_final_stage.reachable_substitute: exact selected-group mean paired difference ONLY for eligible cells (0 own-route text mismatches; eligible seed count reported per task x order), plus group counts, mismatch counts and prediction text-identity counts everywhere
caption_final_stage.selection_bias_note: the route-differ subset is chosen endogenously by the router from item features and caption-instruction form; native would have routed these items elsewhere anyway; the reported paired difference (eligible cells only) is a descriptive counterfactual swap statistic for the selected items, not a treatment effect over a random sample; wording such as 'other-expert benefit' is not implied.

cider_per_image_statement.what_exists: TaskScorer.score (sema_multimodal/metrics.py) returns corpus-level {score, accuracy} for VQA tasks and {score, cider_d, bleu4} for caption tasks; _fixed_cider_score computes a per-image score list internally but returns only its mean; the audit archives store per-file corpus scores only; prediction JSONL rows contain id/prediction/expert/generation
missing_fields_for_absolutegroup_means: per-image CIDEr-D contribution per saved prediction
cider_per_image_statement.consequence: additive fixed-IDF structure is confirmed in code, so caption paired-difference group means are exactly computable from corpus scores at fixed IDF; absolute per-group means are not

note_caption_units: caption rows are CIDEr-D points of the given task (fixed train-IDF); caption family normalized values use the fixed G1 normalizers, matching the document's aggregation

confirmations: zero-delta / no-copy initialization claim of section 1.2 (verified at code level, RNG caveat recorded)
freezing and per-phase optimizer reordering claims of section 1.2/3.3
the exact reported transfer values of section 4.4 (-0.0432397 VQA, +0.0201529 caption) reproduce from the shipped audits under the documented weighting
section 4.5 observation that task-ID-oracle routing is not an upper bound for caption is confirmed quantitatively (family final native 0.7434 > oracle 0.7114; oracle loses on F, wins on C)
conflicts_or_nuances: The caption family positive transfer (+0.0202) in section 4.4 is driven by F only (+0.0924) while C is negative (-0.0521). The independent F reference (0.0999 CIDEr mean over seeds vs normalizer 0.1526) is low in absolute terms; [INFERENCE, unverified] part of the positive F transfer may reflect this weak reference rather than new-task learning. No characterization beyond these numbers is claimed.

The VQA transfer deficit (-0.0432) is roughly half a routing counterfactual (-0.0209 native-vs-own misrouting at the diagonal stage) and half a training-path difference with routing held perfect (-0.0224). The latter has no parameter-level cross-task source per code review; its remaining cause is unverified, so section 4.4's transfer number should be quoted alongside this decomposition rather than attributed.

At the earliest stages the diagonal routing is fully own-expert (position-0 and position-1 VQA rows: 100% own); the visible misrouting appears from stage 2 onward and targets same-family experts almost exclusively (2 cross-family VQA rows across all diagonal cells; 0 for caption).

limitations: No scorer or model execution was performed; every delta aggregates the previously rescored corpus scores already stored in the G4/G5 audit artifacts plus deterministic text/assignment predicates.

Per-example VQA accuracy and per-image CIDEr-D contributions were never persisted, so within-group magnitude splits of the transfer are not identifiable; only the exact corpus-level decomposition (T = R + K), counts, identities and max-magnitude bounds are reported.

R (routing counterfactual) and K (training-path difference) are defined against the same-seed independent runs of the confirmation grid; the 4 fixed orders x 8 seeds only, same as the reported endpoint.

Same-expert rows can produce different text in the native and oracle variant files (counts reported; source unknown), so pool-level subgroup absolute scores and paired differences are unidentifiable; selected-group paired deltas are reported only for eligible cells (0 same-expert text mismatches) with their eligible seed counts per task x order.
Text-identity zero-delta logic is exact for a deterministic scorer regardless (identical text always scores identically); it cannot recover the sign of score changes for text-differing rows.
